sentences.text: Today we will talk about Nauru.
Nauru is a tiny island country in the Pacific Ocean.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Nauru?
Nauru is in the Pacific Ocean.
It is part of Oceania northeast of Australia.
It is one of the smallest countries in the world, only 21 square kilometers.
It is a coral island surrounded by blue sea.
What is the capital of Nauru?
Nauru has no official capital city, but most government offices are in a district called Yarin.
Yarin is where the airport, schools, and parliament are.
Other districts include Iwo Boata Denigamodu.
There are 14 districts in total.
How many people live in Nauru?
Only about 10,000 people live in Nauru.
It is the third smallest country by population.
Most people live near the coast, not in the center of the island.
What language do people speak in Nauru?
People speak Nauruan, the local language.
Many also speak English, which is used in schools, business, and government.
Most people are bilingual.
What is the weather like in Nauru?
Nauru has a tropical climate.
It is hot and humid all year.
There are two main seasons, a wet season from November to February, a dry season from March to October.
Rain helps the island stay green, but the center is often dry and rocky.
What does Nauru look like?
Nauru has a flat coastline with palm trees, a central plateau with old phosphate mines, beaches, lagoon areas, and coral reefs.
The island is small, but has natural beauty.
What animals live in Nauru?
Because Nauru is small, it has few animals.
But you can see seabirds, like frigate birds and terns, lizards, insects, and crabs, fish, octopus, and shellfish in the ocean.
The sea around Nauru is good for fishing and diving.
What do people eat in Nauru?
Nauruan food is a mix of local and imported food.
People eat fish, chicken, and pork, rice, instant noodles, and potatoes, coconut, breadfruit, and bananas.
Popular foods include grilled fish with rice, fried chicken with noodles, coconut desserts, tinned meat, and vegetables.
Because Nauru imports many goods, hand and packaged food are common.
What do people drink in Nauru?
People drink water, tea, and instant coffee, soft drinks like cola or juice, coconut water, fresh and natural.
Clean drinking water can be a challenge, so rainwater is collected in tanks.
What is life like in Nauru?
Life in Nauru is quiet, slow, and close to family.
People enjoy, spending time at home, fishing and walking by the sea, watching TV or playing sports, going to church, sharing meals with family and neighbors.
Many people work for the government or in schools and some work at the airport or shops.
What are some holidays and traditions in Nauru?
Independence Day, January 31st, Constitution Day, May 17th, Angam Day, October 26th, celebrates the survival of the Nauru and people.
Christmas and New Year, church festivals and family events, people celebrate with music, dancing, food, and games.
Some fun facts about Nauru.
Nauru is the smallest island country in the world.
It was once very rich from phosphate mining.
There are no rivers and most water comes from rain or desalination.
Cars and trucks drive around the whole island in under one hour.
Nauru does not have an army.
Now you know many things about Nauru.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about the island, the sea, and the culture.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
